news.story_lead: Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month - Published 9 November 2026 France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month. news.full_article_text: Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month - Published 9 November 2026 France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month. Foreign Minister Jean-NoÃ«l Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions. Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless. The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people". He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act". France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added. The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year. If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran's deterrence strategy. On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets. More than 100 of CoopÃ©rative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from IntermarchÃ© and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe. Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects. In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them. The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations. Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian. news.headline: India’s international air passenger traffic grows despite airspace closures, conflicts
news.story_lead: India’s international air passenger traffic grows despite airspace closures, conflicts Domestic passenger traffic, meanwhile, edged up to 167.4 million in the financial year ending March 2026, a modest 1.1% rise from the previous year. India’s international air passenger traffic grew 6.1% to 78.7 million in FY-26, up from 74.7 million in 2024-25, according to data provided by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). This came despite geopolitical conflicts and airspace closures, which forced Indian carriers to reroute west-bound flights and, at times, cancel them because of last-minute NOTAMs covering conflict zones.
news.full_article_text: India’s international air passenger traffic grows despite airspace closures, conflicts Domestic passenger traffic, meanwhile, edged up to 167.4 million in the financial year ending March 2026, a modest 1.1% rise from the previous year. India’s international air passenger traffic grew 6.1% to 78.7 million in FY-26, up from 74.7 million in 2024-25, according to data provided by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). This came despite geopolitical conflicts and airspace closures, which forced Indian carriers to reroute west-bound flights and, at times, cancel them because of last-minute NOTAMs covering conflict zones. NOTAMs (notices to airmen) are alerts issued to airspace users about time-sensitive changes, conditions or hazards in an airspace. Indian airlines accounted for 44.4% of international passenger traffic during the year, while foreign carriers held the remaining 55.6% share, the data showed. IndiGo had the largest share among individual operators at 20.8%, followed by Air India at 12.9%. Overall air passenger growth rose 2.7% at 246.1 million in the financial year 2025-26, compared with 239.7 million passengers flown by all airlines operating in the country in the previous year. IndiGo continued to account for the largest share of domestic passenger traffic at 63%, followed by Air India at 13.6% and Air India Express at 6.3%. The DGCA data also said there were a total 11 aircraft accidents in Calendar Year (CY) 2025, up from six in CY 2024. One accident involved a scheduled airline, five involved non-scheduled operators and the remaining five involved flying training institutes. The number of serious incidents, however, declined from nine in 2024 to six in 2025. Of the six serious incidents recorded in 2025, three involved scheduled operators and three involved foreign operators. Cargo traffic also registered a sharp increase, the DGCA data revealed, with domestic cargo carried by scheduled airlines rising 24% to 9.78 lakh metric tonnes in FY 26, from 7.89 lakh tonnes in 2024-25. International cargo traffic increased 20.6% to 21.3 lakh tonnes, compared with 17.66 lakh tonnes in the previous year. The international cargo figures include freight only. Revenue passenger kilometres (RPK), a measure of passenger demand, rose 2.4% to 164.3 billion, while available seat kilometres (ASK) – which measures airline capacity – increased 3.8% to 192.9 billion, the data showed. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Neha LM Tripathi Neha LM Tripathi is a Special Correspondent with the National Political Bureau of Hindustan Times. news.story_lead: Sanjit ‘Bunker’ Roy who redefined fight against poverty dies at 81 Social activist Sanjit “Bunker” Roy was decorated with India’s fourth-highest civilian award, Padma Shri, in 1986 Social activist Sanjit “Bunker” Roy was educated at the prestigious Doon School in Dehradun and Delhi’s St Stephen’s College. news.full_article_text: Sanjit ‘Bunker’ Roy who redefined fight against poverty dies at 81 Social activist Sanjit “Bunker” Roy was decorated with India’s fourth-highest civilian award, Padma Shri, in 1986 Social activist Sanjit “Bunker” Roy was educated at the prestigious Doon School in Dehradun and Delhi’s St Stephen’s College. Moved by the hardships rural communities faced, he chose to work at the grassroots and moved to Rajasthan, where he established the Social Work and Research Centre in Tilonia in 1972 to address water and irrigation problems. Roy spent the rest of his life in Tilonia, transforming a small village into an internationally recognised centre for grassroots development, and died there on Tuesday. He was 81. Roy challenged conventional notions of education by centering his initiative around rural communities, particularly women. He founded Barefoot College in Tilonia (Ajmer district), demonstrating that solutions to rural problems did not necessarily have to come from urban experts, government institutions or formally trained professionals. He put a small village on the global development map and demonstrated that some of the most innovative solutions to poverty, energy access and social inequality could emerge from rural communities. Born on June 30, 1945, in West Bengal’s Burnpur, Roy worked on water-related issues in drought-prone villages, including digging wells alongside local communities, after moving to Rajasthan. The Social Work and Research Centre, which later became Barefoot College, evolved into a wider experiment in community-led development, covering education, healthcare, livelihoods, water conservation and renewable energy. The solar electrification project was the initiative’s most celebrated programme. Women from remote villages, many of them illiterate or semi-literate, were trained as solar engineers under this project. These women, popularly known as Solar Mamas, learnt to assemble, install, repair and maintain solar lighting systems before returning to electrify their villages. Roy’s work was recognised internationally. He was decorated with India’s fourth-highest civilian award, Padma Shri, in 1986. Roy was named among TIME magazine’s 100 most influential people in the world in 2010. TIME cited his abiding compassion for the rural poor and said Roy nurtured a grassroots social entrepreneurship that is redefining the way the world thinks about fighting poverty. It noted that Barefoot College has trained over three million people for jobs in the modern world, in buildings so rudimentary they have dirt floors and no chairs. The magazine noted this bottom-up approach is designed to make poor students feel comfortable. It added that the college’s “barefoot professionals” then return home to use their new skills — as solar engineers, teachers, midwives, weavers, architects, doctors and more. TIME noted Roy, who received the Jamnalal Bajaj Award for the application of science and technology to rural development in 1985 and the St Andrews Prize for the Environment in 2003, combines humanitarianism, entrepreneurship and education. It added that he helps people steer their own path out of poverty, fostering dignity and self-determination along the way. TIME said his simple formula holds a key to what nations and aid organisations might do to build a more just world. Tributes poured in as soon as the news of Roy’s death broke. Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot said Roy made significant contributions to rural self-reliance, education and development by following Mahatma Gandhi’s principles. In a post on X, Gehlot said Roy dedicated his life to empowering villages and bringing positive change to the lives of underprivileged sections. Gehlot recalled his longstanding association with Roy. He said he recently visited Barefoot College and met Roy and his wife, social activist Aruna Roy. Congress leader Shashi Tharoor called Sanjit “Bunker” Roy a visionary social activist, pioneer and educator. Tharoor said he had dedicated his life to empowering rural India through self-reliance, sustainable development and grassroots innovation. He said the initiative to train rural women, particularly grandmothers, as solar engineers had illuminated thousands of off-grid homes in India and across the developing world.

news.headline: Bengaluru Chosen to Host Inaugural Standalone Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians Conference
news.story_lead: Bengaluru is set to host the first standalone conference of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians on November 17 and 18. The historic summit brings together female legislators across member nations to discuss legislative leadership and gender-inclusive governance.
news.full_article_text:
### Event Overview
Bengaluru, the capital of Karnataka, has been selected as the host city for the inaugural standalone conference of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP). Scheduled for November 17 and 18, this summit represents a dedicated international effort to address political representation and leadership for women across Commonwealth nations.

### Key Details & Significance
- **Host Location:** Bengaluru, Karnataka, India
- **Dates:** November 17–18
- **Organizing Body:** Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP)
- **Format:** First standalone edition dedicated exclusively to CWP proceedings, moving beyond sessions traditionally embedded within broader parliamentary assemblies.

### Objectives
The conference provides a specialized platform for female parliamentarians to deliberate on structural reforms in legislative bodies, strategies for enhancing female participation in governance, and methods to advance gender-responsive policymaking across Commonwealth jurisdictions.

### Israel Legislative Alignment and Coalition Dynamics

Developments within Israel's parliament, the Knesset, highlight potential political friction for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In a parliamentary system reliant on coalition building, shifts in legislative strength or internal opposition can complicate executive decision-making and legislative passing.

### Governance and Policy Implications

A tight or uncooperative parliamentary majority limits the government's capability to pass key national legislation, including annual budgets, administrative appointments, and security regulations. Managing legislative opposition remains crucial for preserving coalition continuity and executive stability in Israel.

news.headline: CRPF to acquire loitering munitions combining drone surveillance, guided missile strike capabilities
news.story_lead: CRPF to acquire loitering munitions combining drone surveillance, guided missile strike capabilities The Central Reserve Police Force has sought information by November end from vendors what they can supply The paramilitary Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) is set to acquire loitering munitions, or self-destructing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that combine drone surveillance features with a guided missile strike capability, according to a document circulated on Monday seeking information by the end of November from vendors what they can supply. HT has seen a copy of the document. Loitering munitions, which have reshaped modern warfare, have become critical due to their precision.
news.full_article_text: CRPF to acquire loitering munitions combining drone surveillance, guided missile strike capabilities The Central Reserve Police Force has sought information by November end from vendors what they can supply The paramilitary Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) is set to acquire loitering munitions, or self-destructing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) that combine drone surveillance features with a guided missile strike capability, according to a document circulated on Monday seeking information by the end of November from vendors what they can supply. HT has seen a copy of the document. Loitering munitions, which have reshaped modern warfare, have become critical due to their precision. The document, titled Quality Requirements (QRs) and Trial Directives, said the kamikaze drones (loitering munitions) must carry two high-explosive warheads weighing at least 1.5 kg. It added that they must have a range of at least 15 km and an endurance of at least 30 minutes while carrying the payload. The role will be “to carry out one-way missions against designated objectives, using a remotely operated aerial vehicle with a killing/impact radius of 10 metres.” The document directed submission of information by November 25 on the kamikaze drones matching the force’s specific requirement. The CRPF is deployed in Jammu and Kashmir, where the insurgency has waned significantly, and in ethnic violence-hit Manipur. Two battalions of the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA), the CRPF’s elite specialised unit trained in guerrilla tactics, intelligence gathering, and jungle warfare, which were deployed in anti-Maoist operations since its inception in 2008, were moved out for the first time and deployed in Manipur. Militant groups have been taking advantage of the hilly terrain and using drones against security forces in Manipur. They have also deployed country-made rocket launchers with up to a 10-15 km range while hiding in the jungles. The home ministry rushed two CoBRA battalions to Manipur within two months of Union home minister Amit Shah declaring India Maoist-free on March 31 after all top Maoist leaders surrendered, were arrested, or were killed. This coincided with escalating ethnic violence in Manipur, which has left around 370 dead and 66,000 displaced since 2023. People aware of the matter said CoBRA has been involved in almost every major anti-insurgency operation in Manipur over the last six months, and early results have been positive. “CoBRA teams have been successfully reoriented in Manipur. When a militant camp [Sinai] was to be taken over last month, CoBRA was the obvious choice of force to use. CoBRA has been part of all major arms seizures in Manipur since May, as well as the arrest of insurgents in recent killings,” said one of the people. The people said Manipur has requested two more battalions of the anti-insurgency force. “One battalion [around 1,000 personnel] should come soon. In the last six months ...CoBRA commandos [were sent] to every place where the conflict has escalated, and they delivered good results,” said a second person aware of the matter. An official said the regular Central Armed Police Forces will remain posted in the formerly Left Wing Extremism-hit areas, while the specialised unit moves to Manipur and Jammu and Kashmir. “The deployment of a third CoBRA battalion in Manipur will happen very soon, while in Jammu and Kashmir, it may happen in the coming years,” said the officer. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Prawesh Lama Prawesh Lama, an Associate Editor at Hindustan Times with nearly two decades of frontline reporting experience across India’s conflict zones, border regions, and disaster-hit areas. news.story_lead: Odisha Cabinet approves free Wi-Fi scheme for colleges, lifts civil services exam attempt cap Student will be entitled to use up to 1 GB of free internet data daily within campuses for academic purposes The Odisha Cabinet late on Monday approved a series of proposals, including a ₹ 393.62-crore scheme to provide free Wi-Fi facilities across 601 government and aided colleges. It lifted the limit on attempts for the civil services examination for general category candidates and gave the go-ahead to a nearly ₹ 100-crore water conservation project in Balangir. The free Wi-Fi initiative, titled ‘Odisha Shikshanet, Empowering Students through a Free Wi-Fi Internet Facility to All Colleges and Universities’, will be implemented over three years from 2026-27 to 2028-29.
news.full_article_text: Odisha Cabinet approves free Wi-Fi scheme for colleges, lifts civil services exam attempt cap Student will be entitled to use up to 1 GB of free internet data daily within campuses for academic purposes The Odisha Cabinet late on Monday approved a series of proposals, including a ₹ 393.62-crore scheme to provide free Wi-Fi facilities across 601 government and aided colleges. It lifted the limit on attempts for the civil services examination for general category candidates and gave the go-ahead to a nearly ₹ 100-crore water conservation project in Balangir. The free Wi-Fi initiative, titled ‘Odisha Shikshanet, Empowering Students through a Free Wi-Fi Internet Facility to All Colleges and Universities’, will be implemented over three years from 2026-27 to 2028-29. * **Space Ecosystem:** The push for independent launches is part of a broader objective to expand native space technology development, earth observation capabilities, and resilient satellite communications.
* **High-Tech Integration:** Leadership has highlighted the space sector as a key strategic extension of Taiwan's advanced technological and industrial base.

news.headline: Odisha Cabinet Clears ₹4,708-Crore Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project and Removes Civil Services Attempt Limits
news.story_lead: The Odisha Cabinet, under the chairmanship of Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, approved 13 major policy decisions on Monday. Highlighting these choices is a ₹4,708-crore 600 MW pumped storage project in Kalahandi district, designed to provide grid-scale energy storage. Furthermore, the state eliminated attempt limits for the Odisha Civil Services examination and launched the Odisha Shikshanet scheme for campus Wi-Fi across state colleges.
news.full_article_text:
### Major Energy & Infrastructure Approvals

In a key policy meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, the Odisha Cabinet cleared 13 distinct proposals spanning energy, education, agriculture, and public administration. Among the flagship decisions is the establishment of the state's inaugural grid-scale energy storage system: the 600 MW Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project located at Ranibahal in Kalahandi district. Chief Secretary Anu Garg announced that the total project cost is pegged at ₹4,708.64 crore, of which ₹3,371.88 crore is earmarked purely for construction. Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd (MEIL) has been selected to execute the development, with target commissioning slated for the 2030-31 financial year.

The hydro facility is anticipated to generate roughly 1,040 million units of peak power every year. Functioning as a high-capacity energy buffer, it will store excess electricity from the grid during off-peak periods and discharge it back during peak demand hours to stabilize power grid operational frequency.

### Irrigation and Agricultural Welfare Decisions

To enhance water management and agricultural productivity, the Cabinet approved three separate proposals submitted by the Water Resources Department with a total outlay of ₹450 crore. These funds will be directed toward building in-stream storage projects as well as establishing mega lift irrigation units across vulnerable zones.

In agricultural commerce, the government sanctioned the Paddy Procurement Policy for the Kharif Marketing Season 2026-27. The state plans to purchase at least 78 lakh metric tonnes of paddy directly from farmers at a fixed procurement rate of ₹3,100 per quintal. To protect agrarian cash flow, direct financial transfers into farmers' bank accounts will occur within 24 to 48 hours of transaction registration. Additionally, the government extended the operational tenure of approximately 5,000 private fair price shop dealers by one year, extending their validity up to September 30, 2027.

### Administrative Reforms and Student Initiatives

Addressing administrative recruitment policies, the General Administration and Public Grievance Department received cabinet approval to modify the Odisha Civil Services Rules, 1991. The primary change removes all restrictions on the maximum number of attempts allowed for candidates writing the Odisha Civil Services Examination. Aspirants can now attempt the exam as many times as desired until they reach the prescribed upper age cap.

hindi_translation.headline: ओडिशा मंत्रिमंडल ने ₹4,708 करोड़ की ऊपरी इंद्रावती पम्प्ड स्टोरेज परियोजना को मंजूरी दी और नागरिक सेवा परीक्षा में प्रयासों की सीमा हटाई
hindi_translation.story_lead: मुख्यमंत्री मोहन चरण माझी की अध्यक्षता में ओडिशा मंत्रिमंडल ने सोमवार को 13 प्रमुख नीतिगत प्रस्तावों को मंजूरी दी। इनमें कालाहांडी जिले में ₹4,708 करोड़ की 600 मेगावाट क्षमता वाली पम्प्ड स्टोरेज परियोजना शामिल है। इसके अतिरिक्त, राज्य ने ओडिशा सिविल सेवा परीक्षा के लिए प्रयासों की सीमा समाप्त कर दी तथा कॉलेजों में वाई-फाई के लिए 'ओडिशा शिक्षणेत' योजना की घोषणा की।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### प्रमुख ऊर्जा और बुनियादी ढांचा मंजूरियां

मुख्यमंत्री मोहन चरण माझी की अध्यक्षता में आयोजित कैबिनेट बैठक में ऊर्जा, शिक्षा, कृषि और सार्वजनिक प्रशासन से जुड़े 13 प्रस्तावों को मंजूरी दी गई। इसमें कालाहांडी जिले के रानीबहाल में स्थित 600 मेगावाट की 'ऊपरी इंद्रावती पम्प्ड स्टोरेज परियोजना' मुख्य आकर्षण है। मुख्य सचिव अनु गर्ग ने जानकारी दी कि इस परियोजना की कुल लागत ₹4,708.64 करोड़ होगी, जिसमें से ₹3,371.88 करोड़ निर्माण कार्य पर खर्च होंगे। इस परियोजना का विकास 'मेघा इंजीनियरिंग एंड इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर्स लिमिटेड' द्वारा किया जाएगा और इसे वित्तीय वर्ष 2030-31 तक चालू करने का लक्ष्य रखा गया है।

यह सुविधा वार्षिक रूप से लगभग 1,040 मिलियन यूनिट पीक बिजली का उत्पादन करेगी। यह ऑफ-पीक घंटों के दौरान अतिरिक्त बिजली का भंडारण कर पीक डिमांड के दौरान बिजली उत्पन्न करके ग्रिड स्थिरता बनाए रखने में मदद करेगी।

### सिंचाई और कृषि निर्णय

जल संसाधन विभाग के ₹450 करोड़ के तीन प्रस्तावों को भी मंजूरी दी गई, जिनका उद्देश्य नदी-प्रवाह में जल भंडारण परियोजनाओं और मेगा लिफ्ट सिंचाई इकाइयों का निर्माण करना है।

कृषि के क्षेत्र में, खरीफ विपणन सीजन 2026-27 के लिए धान खरीद नीति को मंजूरी दी गई। सरकार किसानों से ₹3,100 प्रति क्विंटल की दर से कम से कम 78 लाख मीट्रिक टन धान खरीदेगी। भुगतान की राशि 24 से 48 घंटों के भीतर सीधे किसानों के बैंक खातों में स्थानांतरित की जाएगी। इसके अलावा लगभग 5,000 निजी उचित मूल्य दुकान डीलरों का कार्यकाल एक वर्ष बढ़ाकर 30 सितंबर 2027 तक कर दिया गया है।

### प्रशासनिक सुधार और छात्र योजनाएं

प्रशासनिक सुधारों के तहत ओडिशा सिविल सेवा नियम, 1991 में संशोधन को मंजूरी दी गई है। इसके तहत राज्य सिविल सेवा परीक्षा देने वाले उम्मीदवारों के लिए प्रयासों की अधिकतम संख्या संबंधी सभी सीमाएं खत्म कर दी गई हैं। अब उम्मीदवार ऊपरी आयु सीमा तक कितनी भी बार परीक्षा में शामिल हो सकते हैं।

उच्च शिक्षा के लिए 'ओडिशा शिक्षणेत' परियोजना हेतु ₹393.62 करोड़ मंजूर किए गए हैं। इसके माध्यम से 601 सरकारी कॉलेजों के 6 लाख छात्रों को रोजाना 1 GB की सीमा के साथ मुफ्त वाई-फाई सुविधा मिलेगी।

कालाहांडी के रानीबहाल में ₹4,708.64 करोड़ की 600 मेगावाट ऊपरी इंद्रावती पम्प्ड स्टोरेज परियोजना मंजूर।
मेघा इंजीनियरिंग एंड इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर्स लिमिटेड को डेवलपर चुना गया; 2030-31 तक पूरा करने का लक्ष्य।

ओडिशा सिविल सेवा नियम 1991 में संशोधन: ऊपरी आयु सीमा तक प्रयासों की असीमित छूट।

खरीफ 2026-27 के लिए ₹3,100/क्विंटल पर 78 लाख मीट्रिक टन धान खरीद का लक्ष्य, 24-48 घंटे में भुगतान।
